vulnerability.name: GO-2026-5932
vulnerability.description: golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp is unmaintained, unsafe by design, and has known security issues

statements.impact_statement: The advisory covers only the golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp packages. /usr/bin/caddy of the image is built from source by the Dockerfile (caddy/go.mod, caddy/go.sum), and the build fails if `go list -deps` of the Caddy main package lists any golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package, so none of them is linked into the binary. Scanners that match by module version (govulncheck -mode=binary, Trivy, Grype) report it because the module golang.org/x/crypto is present for other packages.

zlib comes with the caddy:2-alpine base (Alpine 3.23), whose build with the fix (1.3.2-r1) is not published yet. The only process of the image is /usr/bin/caddy, a static Go binary built with CGO_ENABLED=0: it does not load libz (Go has its own compress packages). In the image libz is linked only by apk and curl, which neither the image nor the self-hosted package runs: the package executes only `caddy reload` and busybox `wget` in the caddy container. The finding goes away when the base image is republished with the fixed zlib; Dependabot then proposes the new digest.

vulnerability.name: GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q
vulnerability.description: Go JOSE: DoS when parsing JWKs that contain RSA keys

statements.impact_statement: github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v3 has no fixed version (the advisory covers <= 3.0.5), and /usr/bin/caddy of the image still links it: the internal CA of Caddy (modules/caddypki) signs with an embedded smallstep authority that is built on it. The finding needs the library to parse a JWK with an RSA key that an adversary controls, and the only place where Caddy takes such input from the network is its ACME server (the acme_server directive, package modules/caddypki/acmeserver). That package is not in the binary: /usr/bin/caddy is built from source by the Dockerfile with its own module list (caddy/main.go), the build fails if `go list -deps` of the Caddy main package lists modules/caddypki/acmeserver or smallstep/certificates/acme/api, and `caddy list-modules` of the image has no http.handlers.acme_server. The embedded authority is used only to sign certificates for the internal CA and never reads JWKs, JWEs or JOSE JSON from a request. Neither the Caddyfile of the image nor the Caddyfile of the self-hosted package uses acme_server or pki, and the admin API of Caddy listens on the container's localhost only. The statement stops being true for a Caddy built with the ACME server, and the Dockerfile does not allow that. Scanners that match by module version (Trivy, Grype) report it because the module is linked; it goes away when smallstep/certificates and then Caddy move to go-jose/v4.
